liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (5 reviews): The second set is built around a strong Other One, then ends with the usual Not Fade Away/Goin' Down the Road sandwich; The Other One runs about 21 minutes and is named a highlight, along with Sugar Magnolia [4][5][6][8][9]
- **Brokedown Palace** (1 review): Called the highlight of the first set, which is full of typical 1971 material [4]
- **Tennessee Jed** (1 review): Reviewer hears a funkier groove in Tennessee Jed than usual [12]
- **Me And My Uncle** (1 review): The Other One, Uncle and Deal sequence is called adventurous, before the usual Not Fade Away/Goin' Down the Road [13]
- **Deal** (1 review): The transition from the Cryptical Envelopment reprise into Deal is singled out as fitting very well [9]
- **Ramble On Rose** (1 review): Early Ramble On Rose with Jerry's vocal phrasing differing from how the song later settled; he seems to enjoy it [8]

## The recordings

- **gd71-10-29.fm.cotsman.10357.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 26 songs; 159 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [1]. Said about its sound: First set sounds very poor for a soundboard, though the second set is much better recorded [15]
- **gd71-10-29.sbd.miller.24999.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 26 songs; 150 min; rated 3.82/5 by 17 [2]. Said about its sound: Muffled soundboard with Keith loud in the mix, though still listenable; Keyboards sit a bit too high in the mix; otherwise the sound is good; Sound quality is not the best but good enough [4][5][12]
- **gd1971-10-29.sbd-set2.gardner.4090.shnf**: soundboard; 13 songs; 75 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [3]

## Around the show

- Show fell on the day Duane Allman died; reviewer imagines the songs were inspired by it [5]
- Venue was the Allen Theater, an old 1920s wide-screen movie house; NRPS opened the show [7]
- Reviewer saw Hell Angels there; atmosphere was relaxed, with a smoking, joking crowd and little pressure on the band [7]
- Pigpen is absent and Keith Godchaux fills in, seemingly playing to impress [8]
- Considered overlooked and perhaps average for autumn 1971, a period when the average was very high [6]
- Setlist stands out more than most 1971 shows, in the reviewer's view [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd71-10-29.fm.cotsman.10357.sbeok.shnf**: source: 1st set: SBD>FM>?>C>Sound Forge>SHN2nd set: SBD>MR>D>CD>EAC>SHNvia Walter Schnell, Tony Gardner & Paul Bottiglio [1]. Also: Listed as taken from an FM source; Truckin' is cut off briefly, while another source has it complete [15]
- **gd71-10-29.sbd.miller.24999.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Recording Info: SBD (7inch Master Reels@7.5ips 1/2trk) -> Cass (Tascam 122mkIII) -> Dat (3800/48k) Transfer Info: Dat (Sony D8) -> RME Hammerfall Digiface ->… [2]
- **gd1971-10-29.sbd-set2.gardner.4090.shnf**: transferred by Tony Gardner; source: SBD>MR>DAT>CDR>EAC>SHN [3]
